mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the pre-tightening period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during such dual-signal months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) above the prior month's level is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
failure_condition: Over 60 such monthly increases fail to produce positive 20-day forward returns in the next 20 days (average return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% over three months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to reduced manufacturing capacity.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers by >1% over the next 60 days with 20-day forward returns not negative.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 5-day forward returns as the market anticipates rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such inflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and a decline in manufacturing payrolls (not directly observable here, but implied by INDPRO decline) predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to weak labor demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive and statistically significant during such dual signals.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 5,000 jobs suggests strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 70% of such months (confidence interval excludes zero).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over 6 months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to persistent supply-side constraints.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers by 2% over the next 60 days with 20-day forward returns not negative.
